newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz increases fire insurance profit. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Allianz increases fire insurance profit. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]

text.p: Allianz suffered a drop in domestic industrial fire business of 11 percent to 652 million marks (corrects from 600 million marks) last year, but improved its gross underwriting result by some 100 million to a profit of more than 70 million marks.
"The decrease of our premium income is certainly partly a result of the present soft market," Manfred Illner, board member of Allianz Versicherungs-AG, told Reuters in an interview.
"But more than half is the result of undesirable business we gave up, or from other intentional measures."

Allianz's share of the hotly contested German industrial fire market slipped to 16.4 percent in 1996 from 17.1 percent in 1995. "However, this is still above the 15.7 percent share we had in 1992," Illner noted.
So far, Allianz had managed to convert around 4,500 of its 13,000 industrial fire policies to the new conditions introduced in 1996.
"We are hopeful that most of the others will follow this year," Illner said, adding that Allianz had two measures in the pipeline that would boost German fire business:

- On 1 April, it will drop supplementary charges within industrial fire policies for things such as the insurance of debris removal, cash or employees' cars in the event of fire. Illner was not prepared to specify the volume this price reduction would amount to.
- The company will also introduce a new product that is closely modelled on all-risk policies.
"It is a modular product, where policyholders can pick and combine the elements they want to buy. The important thing is that all risks are insured within the same framework of conditions."
In industrial liability, premium income rose in 1996 by three percent to 324 million marks, Illner said, and the year had ended with a minimal underwriting loss in this line.
Prices would not deteriorate further in German industrial business, he said.
"Reinsurers are still offering large capacities, but I personally believe that prices are bottoming out, there will be a consolidation in all industrial insurance sectors."
